memo.verdict: Progress to Early-Stage at low priority, as a working hypothesis, not a conviction. Direction: bullish on an eighteen-month view, neutral on a three-year view. Conviction: low. The first test is dated: the H1 FY27 results in February 2027 must show record half-year bookings, a contractor share of the billable base at or below 12%, and a gross margin at or above 30%. The park rule does not bite: management (RA 3, E 1, BB 4) C, business quality (E 2, BB 2) C, predictability (RA 8, E 2, BB 4) B, trackability (RA 7, E 2, BB 4) C; no D or F. At 49.5p (2026-10-09) only the eighteen-month modal path clears the 20% a year bar, by about one percentage point (20.9% a year); the three-year path (15.2% a year) clears only at an entry of about 44p. The record's own summary of the case: a good small business at a fair price whose next eighteen months are underwritten by contract and whose next three years depend on winning the same fight again at a thinner margin; compelling as arithmetic over eighteen months, not compelling as a case for a concentrated book.
case: 1. The thesis. Made Tech is a self-help margin repair riding a public-sector demand recovery: a £74m AIM company selling cleared digital engineers by the day to the UK state, whose next eighteen months are underwritten by a contracted £115m backlog and whose next three years depend on winning the same fight again at a thinner margin. At 49.5p the shares clear the 20% bar over eighteen months on earnings growth alone, by one percentage point, and do not clear it over three years.

2. The change is two-fold and evidenced. Externally, the June 2025 Spending Review gave departments budget certainty to 2028-29 and the Procurement Act, G-Cloud 15, PPN 026 and "Buy British by design" put a sovereign preference behind mid-market UK suppliers and reduced the weight of price in awards; peers confirm the sector-level recovery (Kainos public sector +11%, Digital Services bookings +29%; TPXimpact new business +74%). Internally, management unwound a self-inflicted contractor spike (9% FY24, 19% FY25, 14% H1 FY26, target 10%), hired 108 permanent staff, tightened bid qualification, held administrative expenses to +5.5% against revenue +27%, and stopped capitalising software. There is no chief-executive change: the founder has led since 2008, which is why 'Internal forces' is C and 'Change Forces' B rather than A.

3. The outputs have arrived on every line that matters for EPS. FY26 revenue +26.8% to £58.88m; adjusted EBITDA +69% to £5.89m at 10.0% (from 7.5%); adjusted EPS +72.5% to 2.38p; net cash £14.47m; free cash flow 139% of net income. The £40m August 2026 award took the backlog to £115m and lifted FY27 guidance to £63m to £66m and £6.3m to £6.6m. The one soft line: revenue growth halves to about 10% in FY27 (guidance implies +7% to +12%; consensus FY28 +11.0%), after FY26 bookings fell 37.6%. Under the framework's conditional rule the very positive near-term EPS growth (consensus +28% FY27) needs only plausible logic for continuation: the £40m contract, the promised record H1 FY27 bookings, the 10% contractor target not yet reached.
counter_case: This is a false friend. A record backlog won at tight public-sector rates in a competitive bidding market, carried by a permanent workforce hired ahead of conversion, in a client base where four departments are 57% of revenue and a single fiscal event moves all four. The gross margin has fallen 380 basis points in two years (34.2% FY24 restated, 32.0% FY25, 30.4% FY26) while the backlog rose, against a sector median of 37%; bookings fell 38% inside FY26 and were rescued by one award; bookings have moved -48%, +128%, -38% over three years; the growth rate is halving; AI tooling (30% to 50% developer productivity gains that clients demand back as rate cuts) will shrink the chargeable hours the whole model bills; the finance function has had three heads in three years. The Autumn Budget arrives with £8bn of headroom, August 2026 borrowing of £18.3bn against a £14.8bn forecast, £10bn to £15bn of revenue-raising expected and a manifesto pledge to halve discretionary consultancy spend; FY24 is the precedent, when a procurement pause cut revenue 4% for the year and 7% in a half and the company lost money. If call-offs slip for two quarters, 482 permanent heads become bench cost, utilisation falls to the FY23 level of 68% to 70%, the EBITDA margin returns to 5% to 7.5%, the two brokers cut, and a company-driven multiple falls with the earnings to the 6x to 12x the shares have traded at within five years: the risks research's 22p bear-case fair value is that path, a 55% fall with no dividend to hold the shares. The risks research itself names the low-margin backlog as its highest-plausibility risk; the record's archetype test finds the fit plausible. The multiple has already compressed to the 20th percentile of two years while the price rose 52%, which may be the market saying growth is decaying faster than the record thinks. The mediocrity count is D (38% at A or B; 47% at C), three structural attributes are D (concentration, size, peers), 'Riskiness' is D, the three-year return does not clear the bar at 49.5p, the environment is Double Underweight on Fragility against exactly this kind of name, and a working hypothesis with about a 30% chance of a B-band return is not a use of a concentrated investor's attention: the case should be D and parked, and its crispness is an argument for tracking it, not progressing it. At Setup level, the case may be a mis-filed 'Demand Inflection' whose fit would be D, saying it has no box at all.

The record's concessions, in full: the margin leg is the weaker and rests on execution a business without pricing power must deliver through mix; the growth rate is halving and consensus is not low; riskiness is D for structural reasons no half-year result will remove; the market will not pay for a re-rating in this regime; the three-year return does not clear the bar at today's price; the record cannot refute the own-errors question because no track-record or lessons file was among the inputs; every fact in the park argument is accepted.
triggers: - The dated test: H1 FY27 results, February 2027. Confirm: record half-year bookings; contractor share at or below 12%; gross margin at or above 30%. Alarm: H1 FY27 bookings below £30m; contractor share above 15%; gross margin below 29%. Invalidate: bookings below £15m in any half (Radnor's level); a stated reversal of the contractor policy; gross margin below 28% for a full year.
- Backlog: £115m at 31 July 2026. Alarm below £100m at any report; invalidate below £85m.
- FY27 revenue: guidance £63m to £66m, consensus £63.8m, the record's £65.0m. Alarm: a guidance cut. Invalidate: below £60m.
- Adjusted EBITDA margin: 10.0% FY26; guidance about 10% FY27; consensus 10.0% FY27, 10.9% FY28. Alarm below 9%; invalidate below 7.5% (the FY25 level).
- Utilisation: described, not quantified (the disclosure gap); warning below 72%; target 80% to 85%.
- Debtor days: 46. Alarm above 50; invalidate above 60.
